newsitem.title: USA: American raises ex-US air cargo rates 5-8pct.
newsitem.headline: American raises ex-US air cargo rates 5-8pct.

text.p: American Airlines is raising ex-US cargo rates to Europe, Latin America and selected other international points, including some Japan corridors, by 5-8 percent effective May 1, vice-president cargo sales, Mark Najarian.
AA Cargo rates from Europe to the U.S. are rising by 4-6 percent effective April 1, he said in an interview.
Najarian said the ex-Europe increases vary by country of origin rather than by route.

He said American's cargo traffic remains exceptionally strong. Echoing the experience of other carriers, Najarian said American has seen a good recovery since the fourth quarter of last year in ex-Paris traffic said.

Just about the only negative in the whole AA Cargo international picture is the deterioration in ex-Japan yields because of the sharp appreciation of the dollar against the yen in recent months, he added.
The abortive February 15 strike by American pilots, which lasted but a few minutes, barely dented the carrier's cargo business.
"We were robust up until the day the strike hit, and right after the strike was over, we were robust again," he said.
Najarian said a slight dip in year-on-year traffic could occur in April as the month begins on a holiday weekend.
Apart from that, no decline is expected for some time unless something occurs like the US Federal Reserve raising interest rates to cool off the U.S. economy, he said.
